code: On the title or main menu, press Start 10 to 14 times within a second
effect: Battle Mode's stage list grows from 6 to all 10 stages: In the Gutter, Sea Sick, Blizzard Battle and Lost at Sea are added
note: The title program counts new Start presses in a 60-frame window (50 on the European ROM) and wants 10 to 14 of them with no gap of 7 frames or more; 15 or more in one window fail. The flag at 802AC654 (Europe 802AC644, Japan 802AB884) is set. It is not saved: after a reset it read 0 again, so the code is needed each time the console is switched on. Played on all three ROMs with 12 presses. Picture: the last stage without and with the code.

code: Hold Start while switching the console on
effect: "Is it OK to Erase Game Pak Memory? Yes / No"
note: The boot code tests Start held and loads the erase screen (scene 24) instead of the title (scene 20). Seen on all three ROMs; the Japanese ROM asks in Japanese. Yes was not pressed. Picture: US and Japan.

code: Clear every stage of the first four worlds
effect: Options: the first ???? becomes Music, a music test with 47 numbers (00-46); A plays the number shown
note: The stage-clear code grants this when the best-time slots of all 16 stages of Green Garden, Blue Resort, Red Mountain and White Glacier are filled; the same 16 slots open the fifth world. On the US ROM, with the other 15 times filled in by hand, a real clear of Green Garden stage 1 made the game grant it and save it, and Music was still there after a power cycle. In the test, A turns the number yellow and starts the track (picture: before and after A); the stick alone plays nothing. The music bank holds exactly 47 sequences.

code: Clear Final Battle!, the last stage of Rainbow Palace
effect: Options gains View Credits and the music test, Battle gains In the Gutter and Sea Sick, and music numbers 08, 15, 16 and 44 open up
note: Granted when a stage is cleared with world 6, stage 4 selected; the check reads no difficulty setting. On the US ROM the game granted and saved it when Final Battle! was cleared, and it survived a power cycle; the stage was entered by scene write with the boss's health cut and cheats held, not played through. With only the music-test unlock, those four numbers are drawn as -- and A does nothing (picture: 08 without and with this unlock; 15, 16 and 44 are from the code). On View Credits the A button starts the ending sequence.

effect: Options gains Full Power, and Battle gains all four extra stages
note: Granted at a stage clear when all 120 card flags are set: five cards a stage, 24 stages, no difficulty term. On the US ROM, with 119 card flags set by hand, clearing a stage under its target time earned the last card and the game granted and saved the unlock. Full Power: On, Bomberman keeps remote bombs when he loses a life, and keeps remote bombs, power bombs and blast size above 4 when a stage is started from the world map. Off, the remote bombs go on a death and all three go on the world map. Picture: the same stage start with the option Off and On, the bombs having been given by hand on the world map. It changes nothing in Battle.

effect: The fifth world, Black Fortress, opens on the world map
note: The world map counts the filled best-time slots of the first 16 stages and wants all 16. Shown by filling the slots by hand: with 15 of 16, Up does nothing; with 16 it moves to Black Fortress (picture, US). Run on all three ROMs; the world was not entered that way.

code: Finish Black Fortress stage 4 holding all 100 Gold Cards of worlds 1-5
effect: The sixth world, Rainbow Palace, opens
note: The world map wants a best time for Black Fortress stage 4 and a flag that the stage itself sets when all 100 cards of the first five worlds are held, counting the ones just earned. Shown by setting both by hand: either one alone leaves the map on Black Fortress (picture: without and with the flag, US). Run on all three ROMs; the stage's own card check is from the code.

effect: The 30th enemy drops a Gold Card: the card shown beside Enemies Defeated
note: The enemy-death routine counts kills and drops that stage's fourth card at 30, and again at 60 and 90; the number after Enemies Defeated on the result screen is that counter. The other three pickup cards are inside blocks of the stage, and the fifth is for beating the target time. Shown on the US ROM by setting the counter to 29 and defeating one enemy, with cheats held: the card appeared (picture, with the result screen reading 30). The card was not picked up in that run.

code: Custom: the last three parts of each list
effect: Samurai Head, Clown Smile and Gold Visor, and their matching body, arms and feet parts
note: Each of the four lists has ten parts. The Knight part is there from the first save and six more are pickups. The eighth (Samurai Head, Shogun Kimono, Fans, High Heels) comes with all 120 Gold Cards. The ninth (Clown Smile, Karate Ware, Boxing Gloves, Clogs) comes with clearing Final Battle! while a counter in the save file is under 10801, read as three hours of play. The counter is the file's play time: it goes up once a second, stops in pause and is saved at each stage clear. The tenth, the Gold set, comes with all 120 cards while a second save value is 1 and the play time is at most 10800. With the values written by hand on the US ROM the Gold flags were set at 10780 and 10800, and not at 10801 or with the second value at 0. Nothing was found in the game that sets that second value. The Clown rule is from the code only. Picture: the Head list on a clean save, and its second page with every flag set.

code: Custom: the six pickup parts of each list
effect: Each of the 24 is inside one block of a stage, four to a world
note: Bomb the block and walk onto the part. Green Garden: Dragon Head (stage 1, room 3), Dragon Gloves (1, room 5), Dragon Mail (3, room 3), Dragon Spikes (3, room 4). Blue Resort: Iron Nuckles (1, room 1), Cat Hood (1, room 2), High Tops (3, room 1), Cat Suit (3, room 3). Red Mountain: Slash Claws (1, room 4), Iron Goggles (1, room 7), Rocking Horse (3, room 5), Cat Paws for the feet (3, room 6). White Glacier: Iron Armor (1, room 2), Chicken Head (1, room 3), Chicken Wings (3, room 2), Iron Sneakers (3, room 4). Black Fortress: Drill Arms (1, room 5), Sunglasses and Bubby Socks (3, room 3), Dress (3, room 6). Rainbow Palace: Duck Float (1, room 1), Cat Paws for the arms (1, room 2), Ponytails and Duck Feet (3, room 2). Read from the block table, which is the same in all three ROMs; the notes give each block's cell. On the US ROM four of the blocks were bombed with Bomberman placed beside them by hand and gave the listed part; the routes were not played. Picture: Dragon Head and Dragon Spikes out of their blocks.

effect: Battle Mode has all 10 stages
note: The flag the Start code sets (802AC654, a 32-bit value). Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Battle Mode has all 10 stages
note: The Start code's flag on the European ROM (802AC644). Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Battle Mode has all 10 stages
note: The Start code's flag on the Japanese ROM (802AB884). Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Options: Music, the music test
note: Unlock flag 0 (802A1DA8). Each flag was written on its own on the US ROM; on the European ROM, where the addresses are the same, the three were written together. Written flags are not saved by leaving Options. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Options: Full Power; Battle Mode has all 10 stages
note: Unlock flag 1 (802A1DAC). Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Options: Music and View Credits; Battle Mode has 8 stages
note: Unlock flag 2 (802A1DB0). Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Options: Music, View Credits and Full Power
note: The three unlock flags on the Japanese ROM (802A0FF8, 802A0FFC, 802A1000), written together. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Six bombs at once
note: Player 1's block is at 800AEDF0 in all three ROMs (players 2-4 follow at +C8 each). Bomb count, 2 at the start of a stage. Picture: 2 and 6. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Blast size 6
note: Player 1's block is at 800AEDF0 in all three ROMs (players 2-4 follow at +C8 each). Blast size, 2 at the start of a stage. Picture: 2 and 6. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Power bombs: red bombs with a larger blue-white blast
note: Player 1's block is at 800AEDF0 in all three ROMs (players 2-4 follow at +C8 each). Item bits (800AEE08, 0200 at the start); bit 0 is this one. Picture: the plain blast and the red bomb's blast at the same blast size. Damage was not compared. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Remote bombs: bombs that do not go off on their own
note: Player 1's block is at 800AEDF0 in all three ROMs (players 2-4 follow at +C8 each). Item bit 1. The bombs were still there 260 frames later. 0203 gives both this and the power bombs. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Every bomb bursts in a giant cyan blast
note: Player 1's block is at 800AEDF0 in all three ROMs (players 2-4 follow at +C8 each). Item bit 2, which a timed pickup sets for 1200 frames in normal play. The blast reaches Bomberman from a distance. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Short fuse: bombs go off after 60 ticks instead of 150
note: Player 1's block is at 800AEDF0 in all three ROMs (players 2-4 follow at +C8 each). Item bit 10, one of the seven timed effects of the random pickup. Picture: the same frame without and with it. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Bombs are drawn giant
note: Player 1's block is at 800AEDF0 in all three ROMs (players 2-4 follow at +C8 each). Item bit 11. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: A spare heart: a blast knocks a heart out instead of costing a life
note: Player 1's block is at 800AEDF0 in all three ROMs (players 2-4 follow at +C8 each). Health (800AEE04), 1 at the start. Written once, a hit drops it back to 1; held by the code it stays 2. Picture: health 1 and health 2 in the same blast. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Bomberman's own blast does not hurt him
note: Player 1's block is at 800AEDF0 in all three ROMs (players 2-4 follow at +C8 each). Bit 16 of the state word at 800AEE00, which the game sets for a few seconds after a respawn. Tested against his own bombs only. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: 77 gems
note: The gem count (802AC62C). Picture: the HUD reads 77. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: 77 gems
note: The gem count on the European ROM (802AC61C). Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: 77 gems
note: The gem count on the Japanese ROM (802AB85C). Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: 7 lives
note: Lives (802AC624). Written on the world map: the stage card shows 07. Europe 802AC617 and Japan 802AB857 held the same way through a stage reload; no picture was taken there. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: The stage clock stops at 983, under ten seconds
note: The clock (802AC640) counts hundredths of a second. Held from the middle of a stage on the US ROM. Held at 0 from the moment a stage loads, the clock does stay at 0 but the opening camera never settles, so use a value above 0. Tested as a RAM write in BizHawk, not on a GameShark.

effect: Four test maps left in every version: a checkerboard room, a dark room with stars, a grass and sand map and a small block map
note: The first program archive holds four stage programs that carry the strings "debmap0 : Mapchange happened!", "Playerout happened!" and "Evlevel2 happened!". Nothing in normal play asks for them; the game's start-up value for "next scene" is still 14, but the boot never loads it. Loaded with the scene write below on all three ROMs. Bomberman can walk in each and lay bombs in 14, 15 and 16; in 17 he walks off the edge and is put back.

effect: Jumps to test map 14
note: Map 16 is the only one with its own button check, and the only code in the ROM that asks for scene 14. Played on the US ROM. Picture: map 16, and map 14 after Start.

code: Scene write: 802AC5D4 and 802AC5DC = scene, 802AC5D8 and 802AC5E0 = 10, then set bit 0 of 802AC5D0
effect: Stage warp: loads any scene, the test maps and all 24 stages and bosses included
note: All 32-bit values; Europe is 10 lower (802AC5C4...), Japan 802AB804, 802AB80C, 802AB808, 802AB810 and 802AB800. All 24 stage scenes were loaded on the US ROM, the test maps on all three. A room inside a stage needs its own entry number in place of 10. Picture: Hot Avenger (8A) and Final Battle! (7E).

effect: A one-enemy test room that can no longer load
note: Nothing asks for it. Its program, the same in all three ROMs, sets up one enemy and goes back to the title when no enemy is left, but the collision map it names (564) is now a graphics pack, so the load stops on a purple screen. With that one number changed to another map the room loads and Bomberman stands in it, though it never starts running. Picture: as it is, and with the map number changed.

effect: A six-second jingle that nothing in the game plays
note: Sequence 30 is 920 bytes, seven tracks and 63 notes, and no call in the main program or any of the 95 scene programs asks for it. Recorded from the music test (picture): it sounds for 5.8 seconds, two bars, once, and stops.

effect: Nine music numbers that are all the same 184-byte placeholder
note: Nothing asks for any of them. The nine sequences are byte-identical and stored together at the end of the bank. The music test accepts them (picture: 09). Recorded: one instrument plays a 16-note bar of 1.2 seconds four times, then silence.

effect: An older all-capitals Battle menu left in the Battle program, never shown
note: Battle program, from offset 5AB0: PLAYER 0, OPTIONS, COMLEVEL, NO LIMIT, CHARACTER TYPE, CONFIG, FILE 0, STAGE SELECT, STAGE 0 and Congratulations!. No code points at them; the menu the game shows uses the strings beside them. Same in the European ROM.

effect: Two result-screen labels that neither result screen shows
note: ROM BAC0C and BAC1C, between "Gold Cards" and "Game Over" in the stage-result text. No pointer or address constant for either was found. A stage's result screen shows Gold Cards, Enemies Defeated, Time and Target Time, and a boss's shows Attack Level, Time and Target Time (picture, US); neither label appeared on either.

effect: A pre-drawn 320 x 160 Japanese title logo that no title program asks for
note: Asset 35 in all three ROMs. The title builds its logo from separate pieces, and no call to the sprite loader passes 35. Traps on the file and sprite loaders never saw 35 asked for on any of the three ROMs, through the boot, title, file select, Battle menu, Options, a stage, a Battle and the start of the ending.

effect: Two title graphics still in the US and European ROMs, asked for only by the Japanese ROM
note: Assets 36 and 38. The Japanese ROM loads the Hudson logo at power-on and the copyright line on its title; the US and European ROMs show the licence screen and the "64" in their place. Traps on the loaders never saw 36 or 38 asked for on those two, through the boot, title, menus, a stage and a Battle.

effect: Map information, a thread dump and error messages that can never appear
note: They all go to a print routine that is empty (ROM 24F8). Among them: "*** MAP INFORMATION ***", "Offset:%d,%d,%d", "move.c [Error] : move direction is inadequate 0x%02x", "EEPROM : SAVE DATA REVISION ERROR. PLEASE FORMAT EEPROM. REVISION=%d", "ZeroJump Error : unset segment [ %d ] call[%d,%d]". Build dates: Japan FRI AUG 8 17:45:39 JST 1997, US SAT SEP 6 14:57:59, Europe MON SEP 8 12:04:49.

effect: A routine that matches a list of timed button presses, never called
note: Controller module functions at 80239CC8 and 80239D6C (a "same button again within N frames" helper). The only references are their slots in the module table. The Start code is hand-written in the title program and does not use them.
